samples.text:
The table shows how many grams of six kinds of food people in one country eat each week on average in 1980, 2000 and 2020.

Firstly, bread was the most eaten food in 1980 with 950 grams, but it decreased to 780 grams in 2000 and 610 grams in 2020. Red meat also go down from 650 grams to 520 grams and then 410 grams. Fish was quite stable, it fell a little from 160 to 150 and then to 135 grams.

On the other hand, some foods became more popular. Fresh fruit increased from 540 grams to 700 grams in 2000, and in 2020 it was 760 grams, so it was the most eaten food at the end. Poultry rised a lot too, from 190 grams to 430 grams, and it was more than red meat in 2020. Confectionery went up from 120 to 175 grams in 2000 but after that it drop slightly to 160 grams.

Overall, people eat less bread, red meat and fish, and they eat more fruit, poultry and sweets than before.
samples.why: All six foods covered with accurate figures · simple overview only at the end · rising and falling items grouped but described mechanically · several verb-form and tense errors that do not obscure meaning.

samples.text:
The table illustrates changes in the average weekly consumption per person of six food types in one country over a forty-year period from 1980 to 2020.

Overall, there was a clear shift in eating habits. The consumption of bread, red meat and fish declined, whereas people ate considerably more poultry and fresh fruit. By 2020, fruit had replaced bread as the most consumed item, and poultry had overtaken red meat.

In 1980, bread was eaten in the largest quantities, at 950 grams per week, followed by red meat at 650 grams. However, both fell steadily over the following decades, with bread dropping to 610 grams and red meat to 410 grams in 2020. Fish consumption also decreased, although only marginally, from 160 to 135 grams.

In contrast, the amount of fresh fruit eaten rose from 540 grams to 700 grams in 2000, and continued to increase to 760 grams by the end of period. The growth in poultry consumption was even more dramatic, as it more than doubled from 190 grams to 430 grams, making it slightly more popular than red meat. Confectionery showed a different pattern: it rose from 120 to 175 grams between 1980 and 2000 before falling back to 160 grams.
samples.why: Clear overview highlighting the two key reversals · logical grouping of falling and rising foods · good range of cohesive devices and trend vocabulary · mostly accurate grammar with a minor article slip.

samples.text:
The table details how much of six different foods the average person in one country consumed each week in 1980, 2000 and 2020, measured in grams.

The data reveal a marked change in diet over the four decades. Consumption of bread, red meat and fish fell consistently, while that of poultry and fresh fruit grew. As a result, by 2020 fresh fruit had overtaken bread as the most widely eaten item, and poultry had edged ahead of red meat.

Bread was by far the most heavily consumed food in 1980, at 950 grams a week, but this figure dropped by more than a third to 610 grams by 2020. Red meat followed a similar downward path, falling from 650 to 410 grams. Fish intake was the most stable of the declining items, easing only slightly from 160 to 135 grams.

Poultry saw the most dramatic growth, more than doubling from 190 to 430 grams. Fresh fruit also became increasingly popular, rising from 540 grams in 1980 to 700 grams in 2000 and 760 grams at the end of the period. Confectionery was the only item to fluctuate, climbing from 120 to 175 grams in 2000 before dipping slightly to 160 grams.
samples.why: Well-placed overview identifying both reversals · figures used selectively with accurate proportional comparisons · cohesion managed naturally · precise, varied trend vocabulary · wide range of structures, error-free.
